title: Greek Chicken Bowls
subtitle: Tzatziki, crisp veg, lean chicken
description: Tzatziki, crisp veg, lean chicken. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook 1:1.5 rice to water with salt; fluff and hold covered.

steps.title: Sear protein and veg
steps.instruction: Sear protein in batches over medium-high until browned and cooked through (165°F chicken, 125°F salmon). Stir-fry veg 4–5 minutes until bright with char.

steps.title: Warm the sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk soy and sesame oil; add a splash of rice water if it needs to loosen for drizzling.

steps.title: Assembly line
steps.instruction: Rice, protein, veg, sauce on the side. Greek Chicken Bowls feeds fastest as a build-your-own line.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Build bowls base → grain → protein → toppings so the line moves in one direction.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Greek Chicken Bowls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tzatziki, crisp veg, lean chicken. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
